title: The Sorites Paradox: How Many Grains Make a Heap?
question: If removing a single grain of sand never turns a heap into a non-heap, how can a heap ever stop being a heap at all?
summary: An ancient paradox about vague words like 'heap,' 'bald,' and 'tall' exposes a real crack in logic itself: language is built from concepts with no sharp edges, yet our reasoning tools assume every edge is sharp.
